newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks fall on fear Mideast peace will fail.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks fall on fear Mideast peace will fail.

text.p: Jordanian stocks closed lower on Tuesday plagued by lack of institutional support worsened by worries about the future of Middle East peace, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.34 percent to 147.31 points from 147.80 points on Monday.
A total of 370,522 shares changed hands in 365,179 dinars volume. Of 34 stocks traded, six rose, 18 fell and 10 were unchanged.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flareup in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.
Brokers say the market's plight has been worsened by lack of tangible progress in the Israeli-Palestinian peace process to give impetus after a recent market rebound lost steam.
Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, helped drag the market lower with a fall of 0.750 dinars to 242.00 dinars on very thin trade of 220 shares.
The market was hit by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
Banks led the market on Tuesday, dominated by Amman Investment Bank, which was unchanged at 0.300 dinars on moderate 127,800 share turnover.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.17 percent to 81.05 points, still 15.14 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 206,222 shares worth 97,244 dinars changed hands in weak trade in the parallel market. Of 17 shares traded, one rose, eight fell and eight were unchanged.
